neet_che_u14_t08_1.working: A temporary, complete transfer of π electrons that occurs only while an attacking reagent is present, and reverts when it is removed, is the electromeric effect.

neet_che_u14_t08_2.working: The α-H atoms are 3 + 3 from the two CH3 groups on C+ and 2 from the CH2, giving 8 α-H and so 8 hyperconjugative structures. Some sources add the original structure to get 9; I took 8 as the intended count.

neet_che_u14_t08_3.working: The standard -I order is NO2 > CN > COOH > F > Cl > Br > I > OH > OCH3, which matches option 1.

neet_che_u14_t08_4.working: The tetrasubstituted alkene is more stable. Its 12 α-H give greater hyperconjugation than the 3 α-H of propene, so R correctly explains A.

neet_che_u14_t08_5.working: The Baker-Nathan order is CH3 > C2H5 > iPr > tBu, and tBu has no α-H, so Statement I is correct. Kekulé structures are not real separate species, and the hybrid is lower in energy, not higher, so Statement II is false.
